content_units: Movie Night Shortlist for Four
Context note: I prioritized smart sci-fi, low-gore viewing, runtime under   2h 20m  , and films that spark conversation without ending on a heavy, bleak note.
Best-First Ranking
Rank   Film   Year   Runtime   One-line premise   Why it fits

1     Her     2013   126 min   A lonely writer forms an intimate bond with an advanced AI operating system.   Thoughtful, accessible sci-fi with big ideas about consciousness and connection; emotionally rich but not depressing, and very low on gore.

2     Gattaca     1997   106 min   In a genetically engineered future, a man with “inferior” DNA attempts to pass as elite to reach space.   Smart, discussion-friendly sci-fi with ethical depth, clean storytelling, no gore, and an easy runtime for the whole group.

3     The Truman Show     1998   103 min   A man gradually realizes his entire life is a constructed reality show.   Not hard sci-fi, but highly discussion-worthy on free will, media, and identity; uplifting overall and extremely group-friendly.

4     Moon     2009   97 min   A lone worker nearing the end of a lunar contract uncovers a disturbing truth about his situation.   Elegant, cerebral, and intimate like  Ex Machina , but restrained in violence and compact in length.

5     Contact     1997   150 min   A scientist leads humanity’s response after receiving a signal from extraterrestrial intelligence.   Big-idea sci-fi in the spirit of  Arrival ; intellectually satisfying, hopeful-leaning, and still within your runtime limit.

6     Minority Report     2002   145 min   A cop in a future crime-prevention unit is accused of a murder he has not yet committed.   More action-driven, but still packed with ideas about fate and surveillance; some intensity, though gore is limited.

7     Source Code     2011   93 min   A soldier repeatedly relives the final minutes before a train bombing to identify the attacker.   Fast, clever, and very discussable without being emotionally crushing; a strong pick if you want momentum.

8     After Yang     2021   96 min   A family tries to repair their android companion and discovers the depth of his inner life.   Quiet, reflective sci-fi with humane themes and almost no violence; thoughtful rather than bleak.
Why These Work for Your Group
Option 1:   Her     Best overall balance of smart, warm, and conversation-rich   Strongest all-group pick
Option 2:   Gattaca     Most universally safe choice on gore, length, and tone   Cleanest fit to all constraints
Option 3:   Moon     Best match if the  Ex Machina  fans want a tighter, more cerebral vibe   Shortest “serious sci-fi” standout
Option 4:   Contact     Best match if the  Arrival  fans want idea-driven first-contact energy   Biggest scope, still hopeful
Quick Pick Guide
- If you want the   safest crowd-pleaser  :   Her
- If you want the   smartest classic under 2 hours  :   Gattaca
- If you want the   most intense but still not too grim  :   Source Code
- If you want the   closest vibe to Arrival  :   Contact
- If you want the   closest vibe to Ex Machina  :   Moon
Helpful Notes Before You Press Play
-   Least gore overall:    Her ,  Gattaca ,  The Truman Show ,  After Yang
-   Shortest options:    Source Code  (93m),  After Yang  (96m),  Moon  (97m),  The Truman Show  (103m)
-   Most likely to trigger post-movie discussion:    Her ,  Gattaca ,  Contact ,  Moon
-   One mild caution:    Minority Report  has more chase/action intensity than the others, so it’s the least ideal if “minimal gore” is a top priority
